basis: Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common defining features; other organ malformations vary across duplication subtypes.
Intellectual disability, developmental delay and metopic craniosynostosis define the syndrome; cardiac and intestinal anomalies lack evidence of >=30% frequency.
Tubular aggregate skeletal myopathy; hypocalcemia in 5/5 supports electrolyte involvement. Miosis alone does not establish ocular damage.
Severe cardiac pump failure defines the condition; oliguria, hypoxemia and reduced consciousness alone do not establish lasting extra-cardiac damage.
Hereditary ataxia with defining optic atrophy and sensorineural hearing loss.
Familial structural foot deformity; no additional organ involvement established.
Malignant ovarian tumor of endocrine Sertoli-Leydig sex cord-stromal cells; functional tumors produce androgen excess.
Defining malformations affect the inner, middle and external ear.
Platelet storage-pool dysfunction and oculocutaneous albinism define HPS3; visual impairment is characteristic. Pulmonary fibrosis and colitis are uncommon.
Gonococcal infection defines the mechanism axis; the cervical site has no anatomical axis.
Primary brain-development disorder; supplied HPO marks renal agenesis/reflux and abnormal cortical bone morphology frequent (30-79%), supporting both additional axes.
Defining hair and nail dysplasia, including alopecia and congenital nail dystrophy in 8/8 patients.
Meningioma occupies the lung by definition; it may be primary pulmonary or metastatic, so CNS involvement is not universal.
Congenital shortening and broadening of terminal phalanges define the skeletal disorder.
Severe Rubinstein-Taybi phenotype supports developmental intellectual impairment and characteristic skeletal/limb malformations; other organ frequencies are unspecified.
Umbrella for inadequate vascular or valvular function; no additional organ is consistently affected across subtypes.
Vitamin D excess causes disordered calcium metabolism; renal injury and nephrocalcinosis are complications without established >=30% involvement across the concept.
Inheritance-pattern umbrella rather than an organ-defined disease; no organ axis applies consistently across its heterogeneous members.
Twisting of bowel causes intestinal obstruction and may compromise the bowel wall.
Congenital cardiac shunting and pulmonary arterial vascular disease define the syndrome; pulmonary arteries belong to cardiovascular, and hypoxemia alone adds no lung axis.
Craniosynostosis and intellectual disability are defining features; distal skeletal anomalies reinforce musculoskeletal involvement.
Thiamine transport/metabolism disorder damages peripheral nerves and striatum; muscle atrophy and fixed lower-limb contractures each occur in 2/4 patients.
Human hepadnaviral disease is hepatotropic hepatitis B infection, directly involving the liver.
Nephronophthisis and retinal dystrophy define Senior-Loken syndrome; structural intrahepatic bile duct disease occurs in 4/6. Pancreatic cysts and polydactyly each occur in 1/4.
Cervical vertebral fusion and myopathy define disease; microcephaly and persistent ptosis each occur in 2/2 patients. Cardiomyopathy frequency is unspecified.
